1 ” to allow audio playback *Music* Hallo learner, welcome to a Science and Technology lesson for Grade 4 learners. Today we are going to learn about objects that float and sink. Learner, have a solid and a glass or a basin of water next to you. Your radio teacher is Dominic Muhia. Welcome to the programme. *Music*

2 ” to allow audio playback Hallo learner, welcome to Science lesson for Grade 4. Today we are going to name objects that float and sink in water . Today we are going to name objects that float and sink in water. Learner, I want you to be ready with any solid and a basin or glass of water next to you. A solid is anything we can touch. It can be a pen, pencil, a piece of cloth, a rubber or a piece of stone. Get ready with this solids and a basin or glass of water next to you, I’ll give you time to prepare. *Music* I hope you are ready for the lesson. As we have learnt in our previous lesson, matter is anything that occupies space and has mass. Learner, can you name the three states of matter? What are the three states of matter? Answer when you hear the music. *Music* I hope you have answered. We have three states of matter. The three states of matter are: one solids, two liquids and three gases. We can see, hold and feel solids. Learner, name four examples of solids. Name four examples of solids. *Music* I hope you have mentioned things like stone, book, pen, table, coin, glass and many others. Solids have a definite shape and volume. The second state of matter is liquids. Learner, can you tell me what liquids are? What are liquids? *Music* Good. Liquids are substances that flow and can be poured. Liquids are substances that flow and can be poured. Liquids do not have a particular shape, they take the shape of a container. Liquids do not have a particular shape, they take the shape of a container. Learner, give me an example of any liquid that you know. *Music* Liquids include water, milk, blood, ink, paraffin and juice. Remember, liquids do not have a particular shape. Liquids will always take the shape of a container. If you look at water we cannot talk of a shape of water but we can put water in an oval container or in a cylinder container that way the liquid will take the shape of the container. Learner, now tell me what are gases? What are gases? *Music* Gases cannot be touched but we can feel them. A good example of a gas is air. Gases just like liquids also do not have a particular shape. Gases also take the shape of a container. Learner, what do we call moving air? What is moving air? *Music* Moving air is known as wind. Wind is also a gas. Moving air is known as wind and wind is also a gas. We have different examples of gases. Today I want us to talk about floating and sinking. What is to float and what is to sink? What is the difference between floaters and sinkers?

3 ” to allow audio playback *Music* To float, simply means to occur at the top or at the surface of the water. To float simply mean to occur at the top or at the surface of the water. While to sink means to occur at the bottom of the water. To sink means to occur at the bottom of the water. Objects that float or remain at the top of the water are known as floaters, while the objects that sink or they go at the bottom of the water are called sinkers. So we have floaters which are objects that occur at the surface of the water and sinkers the objects that sink they go at the bottom of the water. Different solids float and sink in water. Different solids float and sink in water. Learner, I want you to take some few solids around you. A pen, a paper, a glass, a leaf, a stone, a coin, a key and I hope you have your basin that is half filled with water or you can use the glass that you have. You can ask your parent, guardian or care giver to assist you. Get the glass and the basin and we want to put these solids and see whether they float or they sink. *Music* I hope you are now ready with a basin or a glass that is half filled with water and some few solids around you. We shall record the things that float and those that sink. Let us put in the solids and we place them one by one and record whether they are floating or sinking. Do that when the music begins. *Music* Learner. Now say the objects that sink and float on water from your observation. Name the floaters and the sinkers that you have observed. *Music* Solids that float on water include: pen, paper, leaf and rubber. A pen, a paper, a leaf and a rubber are known as floaters, this is because they float or they remain at the surface of the water. Solids that sink in water include glass, stone, coin and key. A glass, stone, coin and a key are called sinkers. They are sinkers because they sink or they remain at the bottom of the water. Different solids float or sink on water. *Music* Learner, today we have learnt about floating and sinking. We have said the objects that remain at the surface of the water are floating and therefore they are called floaters because they float while those that go to the bottom of the water are sinking, they sink and therefore they are sinkers because they go at the bottom of the water. T his is your homework. Find other solids that float and sink. Get at least three more floaters and three more sinkers. With that we have come to the end of our Science lesson for today. Goodbye. *Music*

4 ” to allow audio playback That has been a Science and technology lesson for Grade 4 learners. In the program, your Radio teacher was Dominic Muhia.
